The '''Eriadu Conference''', also called the '''Eriadu Trade conference''', or the '''Eriadu trade summit''', was a [[diplomat]]ic meeting that took place on the [[planet]] [[Eriadu]] in [[33 BBY]], in an attempt to solve the long-running power struggle between the [[Galactic Republic]] and the [[Trade Federation]] during the [[Republic Era]]. The Conference turned to disaster when a radical group known as the [[Nebula Front]] not only attempted to [[assassin]]ate [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum]] of the Republic, but managed to [[Death|kill]] the entire [[Directors of the Trade Federation|directorate]] of the Federation. The disastrous events at the Conference ushered in the taxation of the [[Free Trade Zone]]s, which in turn led to the [[Invasion of Naboo|Naboo Crisis]].

==Prelude==
In its last [[Standard century|centuries]] of existence, the [[The galaxy|galaxy]]-spanning [[Politics|government]] known as the [[Galactic Republic]] was engaged in a power struggle with the [[Trade Federation]], a powerful interstellar conglomerate. The point of contention was that the Federation laid down its own law within and around the so-called [[Free Trade Zone]]s of the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid]] and [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] territories, affording special privileges to its corporate partners while forcing independent traders to follow onerous obligations and pay heavy tolls. In effect, the zones once demarcated by the Republic as tax-free had become free only for the affiliates of the Federation.<ref name="Insider 200">{{InsiderCite|200|A Certain Point of View}}</ref>

==The Conference==
[[File:FinisValorum-TPM.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Chancellor Finis Valorum (pictured) was a central figure in the Eriadu Conference.]]
In the [[Standard year|year]] [[33 BBY]],<ref name="Date" /> the conflict between the Republic and the Federation finally came to a head, and it was decided to hold a trade summit on the planet Eriadu. By all accounts, the Eriadu Conference resulted in complete disaster due to the intervention of the [[Nebula Front]], a radical political group opposed to vast corporate conglomerates. Not only did the Front attempt to [[assassin]]ate [[Finis Valorum]], [[Supreme Chancellor]] of the Republic, but it actually succeeded in murdering the [[directors of the Trade Federation]],<ref name="Insider 200" /> among which were several [[Kuati]] executives<ref name="Complete Vehicles 2020">''[[Star Wars Complete Vehicles, New Edition]]''</ref> of the [[Kuat Drive Yards]] corporation.<ref name="Prelude to the Clone Wars">{{EncyclopediaCite|Prologue to the Clone Wars and the First Battle of Geonosis}}</ref> The [[Neimoidian]] [[Nute Gunray]], who already held the title of [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation]],<ref name="JK5">[[Jedi Knights 5|''Jedi Knights'' 5]]</ref> was the sole survivor of the incident.<ref name="Encylopedia Separatists" />

==Aftermath==
[[File:Nute_Gunrays_mechno-chair_-_SW_Episode_I_The_Phantom_Menace.png|300x340px|thumb|right|Nute Gunray rose to power after the Eriadu Conference.]]
The incident at Eriadu had serious repercussions. The [[death]] of the Trade Federation's directorate created a power vacuum that was promptly filled by a group of ambitious Neimoidians. With the backing of a mysterious figure known as [[Darth Sidious]], [[Lott Dod]] and Gunray stepped in respectively as [[Senator|representative]] of the Federation in the [[Galactic Senate]] and leader of the Federation,<ref name="Insider 200" /> while placing like-minded allies in other prominent positions.<ref name="Rise" /> While he had already held the title of [[viceroy]],<ref name="JK5" /> the events at Eriadu ensured Gunray, acting via the viceroy title, was able to assume the role of leader of the Trade Federation.<ref name="Rise" />

Meanwhile, the assassination attempt on Chancellor Valorum gave him a short popularity boost, allowing him to push through a taxation proposal.<ref name="Rise" /> [[Prop 31-814D]] was passed, levying taxes on the formerly Free Trade Zones in the hopes that it would break the Federation's monopoly while also funding the Republic's precarious budget.<ref name="Insider 200" />

Valorum attempted to investigate the summit but was blocked by the planet's [[Governor]], [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], who purposefully prevented the Chancellor from investigating in order to weaken Valorum's position. Tarkin's stonewalling helped to foment and hasten the Trade Federation's [[Invasion of Naboo]], in which [[Darth Sidious]]—who, in his public persona of [[Senator]] Sheev Palpatine, was an ally of Governor Tarkin—secretly engineered the conflict to topple Valorum and become Supreme Chancellor.<ref name="TarkinNovel" />

Acting on the advice of Sidious, Viceroy Gunray retaliated with the [[blockade]] of the peaceful planet [[Naboo]], which itself was in the middle of a dispute with the Federation over the export of its [[plasma]].<ref name="Insider 200" /> Ultimately, the debacle at Eriadu ushered in what came to be known as the [[Invasion of Naboo|Naboo Crisis]].<ref name="TarkinNovel" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Eriadu Conference was first mentioned in the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the [[2014]] novel [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']], by [[James Luceno]].<ref name="TarkinNovel" /> The [[Eriadu Trade Summit|event]] first appeared in the [[2001]] [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] novel ''[[Cloak of Deception]]'', also written by Luceno.<ref name="Cloak">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> The ''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' erroneously states that [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] and [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] met at the conference, with Palpatine persuading Tarkin to enter politics and the latter eventually becoming Eriadu's governor afterward, but according to ''Tarkin'' they had met previously and Tarkin himself was not present at the conference, at which time he had already become governor of Eriadu.<ref name="TarkinNovel" /><ref name="The Star Wars Book">''[[The Star Wars Book]]''</ref>

In Legends, [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] already held the title of "[[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]]" before the Eriadu Conference and simply arose to leadership through the incident.<ref name="DarthPlagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> The canon reference title "[[The Crisis on Naboo]]," claimed that, in canon, Gunray was named Viceroy thanks to the incident<ref name="Naboo">{{EncyclopediaCite|The Crisis on Naboo}}</ref> in addition to assuming leadership.<ref name="Insider 200" /> However, the [[2025]] comic [[Jedi Knights 5|''Jedi Knights'' 5]] depicted Gunray with the title of Viceroy<ref name="JK5" /> between [[40 BBY]] and [[34 BBY]],<ref name="JKDate">The events of ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knights]]'' take place during the time [[Finis Valorum]] is [[Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic]] according to [[Jedi Knights 1|''Jedi Knights'' 1]], but also at least two [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Battle of Naboo]] according to [[Jedi Knights 5|''Jedi Knights'' 5]], as the issue is set "years" before the Battle of [[Naboo]]. As ''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' establishes that the Supreme Chancellor served four-[[Standard year|year]] terms, and the flashback section of [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] which mentions of Valorum's re-election is dated to [[36 BBY]] by ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'', Valorum must have served as Chancellor beginning in [[40 BBY]]. ''Timelines'' also dates the Battle of Naboo to [[32 BBY]], therefore meaning ''Jedi Knights'' must take place between 40 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]] and 34 BBY.</ref> which is before the Eriadu Conference occurs,<ref name="Date" /> thereby meaning Gunray must have already held the title of Viceroy by the time of the conference, as he did in Legends.<ref name="DarthPlagueis" />
